answer: On schema 2025-12-11 the official registry requires name, description and version on every server.json, plus registryType, identifier and transport on each package. Publish (mcp-publisher -> POST /v0.1/publish after /v0.1/auth/*) additionally verifies namespace authentication, package-ownership markers, the public-registry allowlist, and _meta key restriction. Client-verifiable at install: npm mcpName, DNS apex v=MCPv1 TXT, allowlisted registryBaseUrl, and io.github owner/repo string match. Display-only: official.status/isLatest/timestamps, GitHub OAuth proof, the original DNS/HTTP login signature, publisher-provided _meta, and title/icons/websiteUrl. One signal was recomputed end to end: io.github.brave/brave-search-mcp-server mcpName MATCH on @brave/brave-search-mcp-server@2.1.3. SUCCESS:RES-0038 in the receipt AND a signal table split into client-verifiable and display-only with one signal actually recomputed

claims.claim: server.json ServerDetail required fields on schema 2025-12-11 are exactly name, description, version.
Package objects require registryType, identifier, and transport; version and registryBaseUrl are optional in the generic schema but official publish further restricts registryBaseUrl.

Official publish verifies npm ownership by requiring package.json mcpName to equal server.json name. A client can recompute that check: captured io.github.brave/brave-search-mcp-server MATCHES npm mcpName.

Publish authentication is namespace-based: GitHub OAuth/OIDC for io.github.* and DNS/HTTP for domain namespaces, via OpenAPI paths ['/v0.1/auth/dns', '/v0.1/auth/http', '/v0.1/auth/github-at', '/v0.1/auth/github-oidc', '/v0.1/auth/oidc', '/v0.1/publish'].
Domain namespace com.pulsemcp/remote-filesystem still publishes an apex v=MCPv1 TXT on pulsemcp.com, which a client can query independently.
Registry-managed official.status / isLatest / timestamps are display-only: they cannot be recomputed from npm or DNS.
A claim citing only the HTML marketing page at modelcontextprotocol.io/registry/quickstart, with no API or source-markdown rail, would be E3 and must not be cited as fact.

steps.action: init/edit server.json against the published schema
mcp-publisher validate (schema + semantic checks, no publish)
namespace login: github | github-oidc | dns | http
mcp-publisher publish uploads server.json with the login JWT

verifies: JSON Schema compliance for server.json (ServerDetail + Package + transport)
Namespace authentication matches the name prefix (io.github.* vs domain reverse-DNS)
Package ownership markers (npm mcpName; PyPI/NuGet/Cargo mcp-name in README; OCI label; MCPB GitHub/GitLab release host)
registryBaseUrl restricted to the trusted public registries allowlist
Only io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided is kept under server._meta (4KB cap); other publisher _meta keys are dropped

legacy_root.question: What metadata does the official MCP registry require and expose, what does its publish flow verify, and which of its trust signals are actually verifiable by a client at install time rather than merely displayed?

also_recomputed.method: Query apex TXT on the reverse-DNS domain of a domain-namespace server name. Accept only records matching v=MCPv1; k=ed25519|ecdsap384; p=... This recomputes key publication, not the original signed auth challenge.
Compare packages[].registryBaseUrl to the official allowlist value https://registry.npmjs.org (official-registry-requirements.md).
Parse io.github.<owner>/... from server name and compare <owner> to the GitHub repository.url owner. String consistency only; does not replay GitHub OAuth/OIDC.

detail.method: Read server.json name from the official registry API response; GET the npm packument version document; compare mcpName == name and identifier/version against npm name/version.

recomputed_signal.method: Read server.json name from the official registry API response; GET the npm packument version document; compare mcpName == name and identifier/version against npm name/version.

registry_observed.schema_comment: This file is auto-generated from docs/reference/api/openapi.yaml. Do not edit manually. Run 'make generate-schema' to update.

schema_binding.reason: Catalog path is shared with RES-0128, which now owns that file as a coverage-registry schema (required list size 6). RES-0038 pins the freeze teardown schema locally.

signal_table.justification: A client GETs registry.npmjs.org/<identifier>/<version> and compares mcpName to the registry server name. This unit did that for io.github.brave/brave-search-mcp-server / @brave/brave-search-mcp-server@2.1.3 and got mcpName=io.github.brave/brave-search-mcp-server.
signal_table.signal: npm package.json mcpName equals server.json name
signal_table.subject: io.github.brave/brave-search-mcp-server

signal_table.justification: Authentication docs require an apex TXT (not a selector). dig +short TXT pulsemcp.com for com.pulsemcp/remote-filesystem returned a v=MCPv1 ed25519 public-key record. This proves key publication, not the original signed login challenge.
signal_table.signal: domain-namespace apex TXT record v=MCPv1; k=...; p=...
signal_table.subject: com.pulsemcp/remote-filesystem

signal_table.justification: official-registry-requirements.md allows only https://registry.npmjs.org for npm. The captured brave package declares registryBaseUrl=https://registry.npmjs.org.
signal_table.signal: packages[].registryBaseUrl is the official npm allowlist URL
signal_table.subject: io.github.brave/brave-search-mcp-server

signal_table.justification: String check only: name io.github.brave/... vs https://github.com/brave/brave-search-mcp-server. This is not a replay of GitHub OAuth/OIDC.
signal_table.signal: io.github.<owner> namespace owner matches repository.url owner
signal_table.subject: io.github.brave/brave-search-mcp-server

signal_table.justification: Publish uses POST /v0.1/auth/github-at or github-oidc and stores a registry JWT. An installer cannot replay that device-flow or OIDC exchange. Name/repo string match is a different, weaker signal.
signal_table.signal: GitHub OAuth/OIDC namespace authentication performed at publish

signal_table.justification: mcp-publisher login dns|http signs a challenge with the private key. The live apex TXT only publishes the public key. Without the original challenge bytes a client cannot recompute the JWT.
signal_table.signal: Original DNS/HTTP signed challenge that issued the publish JWT

signal_table.justification: Registry-managed. Re-querying the same API is not an independent recompute. Captured brave status='active'.
signal_table.signal: _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/official.status

signal_table.justification: A listing badge. A client that trusts isLatest without fetching /versions is reading a display field. Same-API re-query is still the registry talking about itself.
signal_table.signal: _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/official.isLatest

signal_table.justification: Clock values assigned by the registry. No second rail can recompute them from the package or DNS.
signal_table.signal: publishedAt / updatedAt / statusChangedAt

signal_table.justification: Publisher-chosen JSON, size-capped at 4KB, not authenticated beyond publish auth. Captured brave server.json has no publisher-provided block.
signal_table.signal: server._meta.io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided

signal_table.justification: Schema marks these optional. They are UI. A client cannot authenticate an icon URL or title against namespace ownership.
signal_table.signal: Optional title, icons, websiteUrl display fields

signal_table.justification: The captured npm document carries dist.integrity and npm registry signatures. That is npm's own trust, not a signal the MCP registry required or exposed on this row (no fileSha256).
signal_table.signal: npm dist.integrity / dist.signatures (not an MCP registry field)

legacy_root.strongest_surviving_counterargument: npm mcpName is publisher-controlled metadata on npm: a stolen npm token can set mcpName to any string. The check binds the npm package to a registry name, not to a human identity, and GitHub OAuth is not recomputed at install. The artifact therefore does not call mcpName a full trust root.
